proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(q_0=4+\delta\), and let \(K\) denote a finite positive constant that may change from line to line and depends only on the fixed primitive radii and \((T,C)\).  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\).  Membership in \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) implies all conditions of \(\mathcal M\) and \(s(P)\ge s_N>0\).  Because \(\Gamma^{\prime}\Gamma=I_2\), \(\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\).  Hence, for \(X_{ic}=J_cY_i(0)\) conditional on \(C_i=c\),
\[
\|X_{ic}\|_2
\le \|\Gamma\lambda_i\|_2+\|\varepsilon_i\|_2
\le \|\lambda_i\|_2+\|\varepsilon_i\|_2.
\]
Since \(q_0>4\), Lyapunov's inequality, \((x+y)^4\le8(x^4+y^4)\), and \(\operatorname{ass:moment\text{-}radius}\) yield
\[
\max_{c\in[C]}
\mathbb E_P(\|X_{ic}\|_2^4\mid C_i=c)\le K.
\tag{1}
\]

Let \(N_c=\sum_{i=1}^N1\{C_i=c\}\) and
\[
G_N=\bigcap_{c=1}^C\{N_c\ge Np_\star/2\}.
\]
Because \(N_c\) is binomial with mean \(Np_c\), \(p_c\ge p_\star\), and \(\operatorname{Var}_P(N_c)\le N\), Chebyshev's inequality and a union bound give
\[
\Pr_P(G_N^c)
\le \sum_{c=1}^C
\frac{4\operatorname{Var}_P(N_c)}{N^2p_\star^2}
\le \frac{K}{N}.
\tag{2}
\]
For all \(N\) above a fixed constant, \(G_N\) ensures \(N_c\ge2\) for every cohort. Conditional on the cohort counts, the observations within cohort \(c\) are independent with mean \(\nu_c\), covariance \(V_c\), and fourth moment bounded by (1).  The sample-mean identity gives
\[
\mathbb E_P(\|\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c\|_2^2\mid N_c)
=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(V_c)}{N_c}\le\frac K{N_c}.
\]
Writing the centered sample covariance as the average of
\((X_{ic}-\nu_c)(X_{ic}-\nu_c)^{\prime}\) minus
\((\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c)(\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c)^{\prime}\), and using
\(\|xx^{\prime}\|_{\mathrm F}=\|x\|_2^2\), (1), and Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\mathbb E_P(\|\widehat V_c-V_c\|_{\mathrm F}^2\mid N_c)
\le\frac K{N_c}.
\]
Also \(\mathbb E_P\|\widehat p-p\|_2^2\le K/N\).  Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\sum_{c=1}^C\{\|\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c\|_2^2
+\|\widehat V_c-V_c\|_{\mathrm F}^2\}
+\|\widehat p-p\|_2^2;G_N\right]
\le\frac K N.
\tag{3}
\]

Let \(P_c=I-Q_c=\Pi_2(V_c)\) and \(\widehat P_c=I-\widehat Q_c=\Pi_2(\widehat V_c)\).  The factor law, loading--error orthogonality, and spherical error covariance give
\[
V_c=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
\tag{4}
\]
The first term in (4) has rank two and second eigenvalue at least \(g_\star\).  Therefore, for every rank-two orthogonal projector \(P_0\), spectral decomposition gives
\[
\operatorname{tr}\{V_c(P_c-P_0)\}
\ge\frac{g_\star}{2}\|P_c-P_0\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\tag{5}
\]
The projector \(\widehat P_c\) maximizes \(P_0\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\widehat V_cP_0)\) over rank-two projectors. Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{tr}\{V_c(P_c-\widehat P_c)\}
&\le \operatorname{tr}\{(V_c-\widehat V_c)(P_c-\widehat P_c)\}\\
&\le \|V_c-\widehat V_c\|_{\mathrm F}
       \|P_c-\widehat P_c\|_{\mathrm F}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining this display with (5), including the trivial case \(P_c=\widehat P_c\), proves
\[
\|\widehat Q_c-Q_c\|_{\mathrm F}
\le \frac{2}{g_\star}\|\widehat V_c-V_c\|_{\mathrm F}.
\tag{6}
\]

Use the padded matrices
\[
\mathcal R=\operatorname{stack}_{c=1}^C\sqrt{p_c}\,Q_cJ_c,
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal R}
=\operatorname{stack}_{c=1}^C\sqrt{\widehat p_c}\,\widehat Q_cJ_c.
\]
Their Gram matrices are \(A(P)\) and \(\widehat A\).  On \(G_N\), both \(p_c\) and \(\widehat p_c\) are bounded below by a positive constant.  The identity
\[
\sqrt{\widehat p_c}\widehat Q_c-\sqrt{p_c}Q_c
=\sqrt{\widehat p_c}(\widehat Q_c-Q_c)
+(\sqrt{\widehat p_c}-\sqrt{p_c})Q_c,
\]
the bound
\(|\sqrt x-\sqrt y|=|x-y|/(\sqrt x+\sqrt y)\), (3), and (6) imply
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left(
\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}^2;G_N
\right)\le\frac K N.
\tag{7}
\]

Equation (4) implies \(Q_c\Gamma_{S_c}=0\) for every \(c\), so
\(\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\subseteq\ker\mathcal R\).  Because
\(s(P)=\sigma_{T-2}(\mathcal R)\ge s_N>0\) and \(\Gamma\) has rank two, \(\mathcal R\) has rank \(T-2\) and
\[
\ker\mathcal R=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma).
\tag{8}
\]
Let \(U\) be an orthonormal basis of this kernel.  Since \(\widehat U\) consists of the bottom two right singular vectors of \(\widehat{\mathcal R}\), its variational optimality, with \(U\) as competitor, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\mathcal R\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}
&\le \|(\mathcal R-\widehat{\mathcal R})\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}
     +\|\widehat{\mathcal R}\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\le \sqrt2\|\mathcal R-\widehat{\mathcal R}\|_{\mathrm F}
     +\|\widehat{\mathcal R}U\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\le2\sqrt2\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The restriction of \(\mathcal R\) to \(\operatorname{col}(U)^\perp\) has smallest singular value at least \(s_N\). Hence
\[
E_U:=\|(I-UU^{\prime})\widehat U\|_{\mathrm F}
\le\frac{2\sqrt2}{s_N}
\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}.
\tag{9}
\]

The covariance upper bound and local signal gap imply
\[
g_\star
\le\lambda_2(\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime})
\le v^\star\sigma_2(\Gamma_{S_c})^2,
\qquad
\sigma_2(U_{S_c})\ge a:=\sqrt{g_\star/v^\star}>0.
\tag{10}
\]
The principal-angle singular-value decomposition supplies an orthogonal \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix \(W\) such that, for \(\widetilde U=\widehat UW\),
\[
\|\widetilde U-U\|_{\mathrm F}^2
=2\sum_{j=1}^2(1-\cos\phi_j)
\le2\sum_{j=1}^2\sin^2\phi_j
=2E_U^2.
\tag{11}
\]
If \(E_U\le a/(4\sqrt2)\), Weyl's singular-value inequality and (11) give
\(\sigma_2(\widetilde U_{S_c})\ge a/2\) for every \(c\).  Define
\[
K_c(X)=X(X_{S_c}^{\prime}X_{S_c})^{-1}X_{S_c}^{\prime}.
\]
Whenever the inverse exists, right-orthogonal invariance gives
\(K_c(\widehat U)=K_c(\widehat UW)=K_c(\widetilde U)\).
For \(X=U\) and \(X=\widetilde U\), (10)--(11) bound the displayed inverses uniformly.  Applying
\[
G^{-1}-\widetilde G^{-1}=G^{-1}(\widetilde G-G)\widetilde G^{-1}
\]
to \(G=U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c}\) and
\(\widetilde G=\widetilde U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widetilde U_{S_c}\), then expanding the three factors in \(K_c\), yields
\[
\|K_c(\widetilde U)-K_c(U)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le K\|\widetilde U-U\|_{\mathrm F}
\le K E_U.
\tag{12}
\]
By the factor law and conditional mean-zero error,
\(\nu_c=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c\).  Since \(U=\Gamma W_0\) for an orthogonal \(W_0\), this identity and full column rank of \(U_{S_c}\) imply
\[
K_c(U)\nu_c=\Gamma m_c=\mu_c(P).
\tag{13}
\]
The effective-radius lemma gives \(\|m_c\|_2\le b_\lambda\), so \(\|\nu_c\|_2\le b_\lambda\), which is bounded by the fixed primitive radii.  On \(G_N\cap\{E_U\le a/(4\sqrt2)\}\), the raw least-squares branch exists, and (9), (12), and (13) give
\[
\|K_c(\widetilde U)\widehat\nu_c-\mu_c(P)\|_2
\le K\left\{
\|\widehat\nu_c-\nu_c\|_2
+\frac{\|\widehat{\mathcal R}-\mathcal R\|_{\mathrm F}}{s_N}
\right\}.
\tag{14}
\]
Clipping to \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^T\) cannot increase coordinatewise distance from \(\mu_c(P)\), because the effective-radius lemma places every target coordinate in that interval.  Thus (14), (3), and (7) show that the expected squared sup-norm error on this event is at most \(K/(Ns_N^2)\).  By (2), (7), (9), and Markov's inequality, the complement has probability at most
\[
\Pr_P(G_N^c)
+\Pr_P\{E_U>a/(4\sqrt2),G_N\}
\le\frac K N+\frac{K}{Ns_N^2}
\le\frac{K}{Ns_N^2},
\tag{15}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(s_N\le1\).  The loss is at most one on the complement, including every prescribed zero-fallback sample.  Combining (14)--(15) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PL(\widehat\mu,\mu(P))
\le\frac{K}{Ns_N^2}
\tag{16}
\]
for all \(N\) above a fixed constant.  Enlarging \(K\) proves (16) for the finitely many smaller \(N\), because \(s_N\le1\) and \(L\le1\).

Finally, both branches of the corrected estimator lie in \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\), and the effective-radius lemma puts \(\mu(P)\) in the same box.  Therefore, deterministically,
\[
L(\widehat\mu,\mu(P))
\le\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2\}.
\tag{17}
\]
Taking the minimum of (16) and (17) proves the stated bound, uniformly over the shell.

For each \(N\), define
\[
R_N=
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}.
\]
Nonnegativity of the loss and \(\operatorname{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) give
\[
0\le R_N
\le \min\!\left\{1,4b_\lambda^2,\frac{C_0}{Ns_N^2}\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\), the last entry of the minimum in (1) tends to zero, so the squeeze theorem yields \(R_N\to0\).  This proves sufficiency.

To prove that the condition is not necessary, invoke \(\operatorname{thm:four\text{-}mask\text{-}early\text{-}kill\text{-}negative}\).  It supplies allowed fixed primitive radii, a legal equal-share four-mask family \((P_\eta)\), and constants \(a_0,a_1,\eta_0>0\) such that
\[
a_0|\eta|\le s(P_\eta)\le a_1|\eta|
\quad\text{for }0<|\eta|\le\eta_0,
\qquad
\mu(P)=0
\quad\text{for every law in that model}.
\tag{2}
\]
Set
\[
\eta_N=\frac{\eta_0}{N+1},
\qquad
s_N=s(P_{\eta_N}).
\tag{3}
\]
The first inequality in (2) gives \(s_N>0\).  To verify \(s_N\le1\), take any \(x\in\mathbb R^T\).  By \(\operatorname{def:relation\text{-}operator}\), \(0\preceq Q_c\preceq I_{|S_c|}\), and \(\sum_cp_c=1\),
\[
x^{\prime}A(P)x
=\sum_{c=1}^Cp_c\|Q_cJ_cx\|_2^2
\le\sum_{c=1}^Cp_c\|J_cx\|_2^2
\le\|x\|_2^2.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(A(P)\preceq I_T\), and \(\operatorname{def:relation\text{-}margin}\) implies \(s(P)\le1\).  By (3), \(s_N\in(0,1]\), and
\[
s_N\le s(P_{\eta_N})=s_N\le2s_N,
\]
so \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\).  Every shell in the sequence is therefore nonempty.  The upper inequality in (2) gives
\[
Ns_N^2
\le \frac{Na_1^2\eta_0^2}{(N+1)^2}
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]
Every law in \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) belongs to the same zero-target ambient model, so the identically zero estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PL\{0,\mu(P)\}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
By nonnegativity, (6) implies \(R_N=0\) for every \(N\), whereas (5) gives \(Ns_N^2\to0\).  Hence the sufficient condition is not necessary under the frozen assumptions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every \(c\in[C]\),
\[
\|m_c\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(H_c)\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0},
\qquad
\|m_c\|_2\le b_\lambda,
\qquad
\max_{t\in[T]}|\mu_{ct}(P)|\le b_\lambda.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(c\in[C]\).  The exponent \(q_0=4+\delta\) in \(\operatorname{def:effective\text{-}loading\text{-}mean\text{-}radius}\) is larger than two because \(\delta>0\).  By the definition of the conditional mean and covariance,
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left(\|\lambda_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c\right)
=\|m_c\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(H_c).
\tag{1}
\]
Lyapunov's inequality, followed by the nonnegativity of the error moment and \(\operatorname{ass:moment\text{-}radius}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\{\|m_c\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(H_c)\right\}^{q_0/2}
&=\left\{\mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)\right\}^{q_0/2}\\
&\le \mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)\\
&\le \mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}+\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)\\
&\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Taking the power \(2/q_0>0\) in (2) proves the first displayed inequality in the statement.  By \(\operatorname{ass:loading\text{-}covariance}\), both eigenvalues of \(H_c\) are at least \(v_\star\), and therefore
\[
\operatorname{tr}(H_c)\ge 2v_\star.
\tag{3}
\]
Combining (2)--(3) yields
\[
\|m_c\|_2^2
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star.
\tag{4}
\]
The left side of (4) is nonnegative.  Hence the right side is nonnegative for every nonempty model, and the definition of \(b_\lambda\) gives \(\|m_c\|_2\le b_\lambda\).  Finally, \(\operatorname{ass:factor\text{-}normalization}\) implies \(\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\).  Since \(\mu_c(P)=\Gamma m_c\), for each \(t\in[T]\),
\[
|\mu_{ct}(P)|
=|e_t^{\prime}\Gamma m_c|
\le \|e_t^{\prime}\Gamma\|_2\|m_c\|_2
\le \|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|m_c\|_2
\le b_\lambda.
\]
This proves all three assertions.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Estimate \(\nu_c\) and \(V_c\) by cohort sample moments, form \(\widehat Q_c=I-\Pi_2(\widehat V_c)\) and \(\widehat A=\sum_c\widehat p_cJ_c^{\prime}\widehat Q_cJ_c\), and take \(\widehat U\) as its bottom two eigenvectors, using fixed deterministic Borel tie-breaking conventions for every eigenspace and basis. Whenever all required cohort moments and inverses exist, set
\[
\widehat\mu_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^T}\!\left\{\widehat U(\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat U_{S_c})^{-1}\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat\nu_c\right\}.
\]
If a required cohort moment is unavailable or any displayed inverse does not exist, set the entire vector \(\widehat\mu\) equal to zero. Thus the construction is everywhere a measurable element of \(\mathbb R^{C\times T}\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The primitive moment restriction and covariance floor imply the smaller coordinate radius \(b_\lambda\); clipping at \(B\) discards this available maximality information.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: Every feasible target lies in \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\), so both the profiled rectangle and the total small-sample fallback must use that effective target box.

prose_updates.tldr: Short panels with systematic missing outcomes require gluing cohort-specific covariance eigenspaces before missing untreated means become causal functionals. A deterministic smallest-two anchor convention maps every mask to the published rank-two count certificate, with pebble recognition and extraction as background. Certificate acceptance yields an explicit complete-observed-law map; certificate failure yields generic factor-plane nonuniqueness but not model-wide causal-target nonidentification. For the stochastic class studied here, put \(q_0=4+\delta\) and \(b_\lambda=(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star)_+^{1/2}\). Covariance PCA has unconditional squared-risk upper bound \(\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2,C_0/(Ns_N^2)\}\), and robust profile-recentered inversion has uniform coverage with maximal half-width at most \(\min\{b_\lambda,C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\}\). The four-mask witness shows strict geometric containment beyond \(O_3\). No universal lower frontier or necessity claim is made: \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient, while an allowed boundary class has \(b_\lambda=0\) and zero target throughout.

project_justification.gap: Published matrix-completion count criteria and pebble algorithms certify generic rank-two geometry, while Lei and Ross provide an \(O_3\)-sufficient APM analysis. They do not give the complete-observed-law causal transport proved here, nor the radius-adaptive finite-sample upper guarantees \(\min\{1,4b_\lambda^2,C_0/(Ns_N^2)\}\) and \(\min\{b_\lambda,C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\}\). The stochastic class here is not literally the full Lei--Ross class: the overlap is only the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error intersection subclass, and \(O_3\) is used geometrically.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies fixed-\(T\) causal recovery under deterministic cohort masks, separating generic factor-plane certification from causal-target identification and separating singular-margin instability from the smaller target radius forced by the primitive moment budget. It combines an explicit observed-law functional, strict \(O_3\) containment, covariance--PCA risk upper bounds, and finite-moment uniformly honest moment inversion.
project_justification.fill: The paper takes the published count and pebble results as inputs, proves positive causal transport when the certificate passes, and records only factor-plane ambiguity when it fails. It derives \(\|m_c\|_2\le b_\lambda\) from the frozen moment and covariance restrictions, clips estimation and inversion to the resulting target box, and proves radius-adaptive unconditional upper guarantees. Nondegenerate same-shell testing pairs and corresponding lower risk and width frontiers remain open.

sampling_model.design: Observational short panel with deterministic cohort-specific untreated masks \(S_c\) and independent cross-sectional sampling. The model analyzed here is the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error intersection subclass of the broader Lei--Ross environment, not that full stochastic class.
sampling_model.treatment: For cohort \(c\), recovery uses \(J_cY_i(0)\). The untreated factor law has conditional mean-zero, loading-uncorrelated, spherical errors; treated outcomes are outside the recovery functional and may be appended without changing it.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \(p_c\ge p_\star>0\) and every \(S_c\) contains at least three coordinates. Identification strength is the observable relation margin \(s(P)\), while feasible target size is bounded by \(b_\lambda=(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/(4+\delta)}-2v_\star)_+^{1/2}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cohort means and covariances feed covariance PCA and APM least squares, clipped to \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\). Robust joint-moment blocks feed a profile-recentered compact-model inversion whose rectangle is intersected with the same box. Both procedures are total, and the results are unconditional upper guarantees rather than lower-frontier claims.

prose_updates.related_work: Published deterministic rank-two sampling criteria and sparse-hypergraph pebble algorithms provide the geometric certificate, while determinantal-matroid work explains generic completion. Lei and Ross are the closest econometric comparator, but the stochastic class in this paper is not their full class: only the no-covariate, no-fixed-effect, strictly exogenous, spherical-error intersection subclass is shared. Their \(O_3\) procedure is used as a geometric sufficient screen; the masks \(123,145,256,346\) show strict certificate inclusion. The distinct causal contribution is the complete-observed-law mean functional and the radius-adaptive upper analysis. Projection perturbation results explain reciprocal-margin behavior but do not furnish a legal target-separating experiment under the frozen primitives. Growing staggered-matrix inference, weak-factor honesty theory, and general identification-robust inference likewise do not close the missing nondegenerate same-shell lower construction. The \(\operatorname{apm}\) Veneto counterfactual-wage workflow and \(\operatorname{fect}\) are consumers, not assertions that their full maintained models coincide with this class.
prose_updates.interpretation: The relation margin \(s(P)\) measures the stability of gluing local factor planes, whereas \(b_\lambda\) measures how far the primitive moment budget permits cohort loading means, and hence counterfactual means, to move. The two restrictions act through different minima: sampling instability contributes \(1/(Ns_N^2)\) to squared risk and \(1/(\sqrt N s_N)\) to half-width, while the target box contributes \(4b_\lambda^2\) and \(b_\lambda\), respectively. Thus a small relation margin is a conservative warning, not an impossibility certificate when the target radius is itself small or zero.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Certificate failure proves generic factor-plane nonuniqueness but not distinct causal targets under the frozen primitive class. At the nonempty-model moment boundary \(b_\lambda=0\), equivalently \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v_\star)^{(4+\delta)/2}\), the strengthened boundary argument forces \(H_c=v_\star I_2\), \(m_c=0\), and zero errors almost surely, so every causal target is zero. Shell nonemptiness alone therefore supplies neither target separation nor primitive interior slack. Construction of a nondegenerate frontier-scale testing pair and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open. The covariance--PCA and robust-inversion results are unconditional upper guarantees; numerical certification of the compact profile optimization is outside the theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The deterministic anchor convention, generic rank-two count criterion, and pebble algorithms are published geometric background. The paper claims positive causal transport from certificate acceptance, strict geometric containment beyond \(O_3\), and radius-adaptive unconditional upper guarantees for the stated spherical-error factor subclass. It does not identify this stochastic class with the full Lei--Ross model. The point estimator clips to \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\), and robust moment inversion intersects its profiled rectangle with the same box while retaining total fallbacks. No minimax lower frontier, honest-width lower frontier, causal-target converse on certificate failure, or necessity of \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is claimed.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(N\in\mathbb N\) and \(s_N\in(0,1]\) such that \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\ne\varnothing\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\). The support condition \(p_c\ge p_\star>0\) in \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}shares}\) makes every cohort-conditional moment below well defined. Put \(q_0=4+\delta>4\), as in \(\mathrm{def:effective\text{-}loading\text{-}mean\text{-}radius}\), and let
\[
\vartheta_0=\bigl(p,\Gamma,(m_c,H_c,\sigma_c)_{c=1}^C\bigr)
\]
be the primitive parameter induced by \(P\).

We first establish the effective-radius bound, including the positivity needed to take its square root. For every \(c\in[C]\), the covariance identity and \(\mathrm{ass:loading\text{-}covariance}\) give
\[
\mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)
=\operatorname{tr}(H_c)+\|m_c\|_2^2
\ge 2v_\star+\|m_c\|_2^2.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(q_0>2\), Lyapunov's inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:moment\text{-}radius}\) imply
\[
\left(2v_\star+\|m_c\|_2^2\right)^{q_0/2}
\le \left\{\mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)\right\}^{q_0/2}
\le \mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}.
\tag{2}
\]
Taking the increasing power \(2/q_0\) in (2) yields
\[
0\le\|m_c\|_2^2
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star,
\qquad
\|m_c\|_2\le b_\lambda.
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, nonemptiness of the model implies \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star\ge0\), so the positive-part operation in the definition of \(b_\lambda\) does not alter the right side for any admissible law. By \(\mathrm{ass:rank\text{-}two\text{-}factor\text{-}law}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:error\text{-}mean}\),
\[
\mu_c(P)=\mathbb E_P\{Y_i(0)\mid C_i=c\}=\Gamma m_c.
\tag{4}
\]
The normalization \(\Gamma^{\prime}\Gamma=I_2\) in \(\mathrm{ass:factor\text{-}normalization}\) gives \(\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\) and hence \(\|\Gamma_{t\cdot}\|_2\le1\). Equations (3)--(4) therefore give
\[
|\mu_{ct}(P)|=|\Gamma_{t\cdot}m_c|
\le\|\Gamma_{t\cdot}\|_2\|m_c\|_2
\le b_\lambda
\quad(c\in[C],\ t\in[T]).
\tag{5}
\]
The same bound applies to every \(\vartheta\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\). Indeed, by the closure in \(\mathrm{def:primitive\text{-}moment\text{-}class}\), choose primitive points \(\vartheta^{(r)}\) before closure with \(\vartheta^{(r)}\to\vartheta\). At every such point, membership of \(m^{(r)}\) in \(\mathfrak M_\lambda(H^{(r)})\) supplies, for each \(c\), a loading law having mean \(m_c^{(r)}\), covariance \(H_c^{(r)}\), and \(q_0\)-moment at most \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}\), while the primitive constraints give \(H_c^{(r)}\succeq v_\star I_2\) and \((\Gamma^{(r)})^{\prime}\Gamma^{(r)}=I_2\). Repeating (1)--(5) gives \(|(\Gamma^{(r)}m_c^{(r)})_t|\le b_\lambda\). Continuity of matrix multiplication and closedness of \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\) then yield
\[
(\Gamma m_c)_{c=1}^C\in[-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}
\quad\text{for every }\vartheta\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N).
\tag{6}
\]

We next verify feasibility of the true primitive parameter. By \(\mathrm{ass:error\text{-}mean}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}homoskedasticity}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)
=\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_i\mid C_i=c)\}
=T\sigma_c^2.
\]
Another application of Lyapunov's inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:moment\text{-}radius}\) gives
\[
(T\sigma_c^2)^{q_0/2}
\le \mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}},
\qquad
0\le\sigma_c\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{1/q_0}/\sqrt T\le B.
\tag{7}
\]
The actual conditional law of \(\lambda_i\) witnesses \(m\in\mathfrak M_\lambda(H)\). Equation (7), the share, normalization, covariance, and local-eigengap restrictions in \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}shares}\), \(\mathrm{ass:factor\text{-}normalization}\), \(\mathrm{ass:loading\text{-}covariance}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:local\text{-}signal\text{-}gap}\), and the inequalities \(s_N\le s(P)\le2s_N\) in \(\mathrm{ass:singular\text{-}shell}\) verify every constraint in \(\mathrm{def:primitive\text{-}moment\text{-}class}\). Thus
\[
\vartheta_0\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N).
\tag{8}
\]

We now relate the observed-law moment map to the causal target, rather than defining them to be equal. From the factor law and conditional mean-zero error,
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c\}=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.
\tag{9}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{ass:loading\text{-}error\text{-}orthogonality}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:error\text{-}mean}\) give
\[
\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\varepsilon_i^{\prime}\mid C_i=c)
=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\lambda_i,\varepsilon_i\mid C_i=c)
+m_c\mathbb E_P(\varepsilon_i^{\prime}\mid C_i=c)=0,
\tag{10}
\]
and the transposed cross moment also vanishes. Since
\(\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\lambda_i^{\prime}\mid C_i=c)=H_c+m_cm_c^{\prime}\), conditional homoskedasticity and (10) imply
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)Y_i(0)^{\prime}J_c^{\prime}\mid C_i=c\}
=\Gamma_{S_c}(H_c+m_cm_c^{\prime})\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}
+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
\tag{11}
\]
Multiplying (9) and (11) by \(p_c\), and adjoining the indicator moment \(p_c\), reproduces coordinate by coordinate the map in \(\mathrm{def:moment\text{-}inversion}\). Hence
\[
g(\vartheta_0)=\theta(P),
\tag{12}
\]
whereas (4) identifies the causal mean represented by \(\vartheta_0\). This proves the required observed-law-to-target relationship.

Suppose first that \(N\ge2k_\alpha\), and define
\[
E_N=\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m},
\qquad
\mathcal E_N=\{E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\}.
\]
Compactness of \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\) makes the profiled minimum attainable. From (8), (12), and the definition of \(d_N\),
\[
d_N\le\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}=E_N.
\tag{13}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N\), equations (12)--(13) show
\[
\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\le d_N+\widehat\rho_N,
\]
so \(\vartheta_0\in\mathcal C_N\). Thus the raw enclosing rectangle contains \(\mu(P)\) by (4), and the effective-radius box contains \(\mu(P)\) by (5). Their intersection therefore contains \(\mu(P)\) on \(\mathcal E_N\). The coverage part of \(\mathrm{lem:robust\text{-}moment\text{-}ball}\) yields
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\Pr_P\{\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\}
\ge\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\Pr_P(\mathcal E_N)
\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{14}
\]
When \(N<2k_\alpha\), the corrected construction returns \([-b_\lambda,b_\lambda]^{CT}\), which covers with probability one by (5). Hence (14) holds for every \(N\).

For completeness, we verify measurability of the inversion. Set \(K_N=\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\). It is a nonempty compact subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space by (8) and \(\mathrm{def:primitive\text{-}moment\text{-}class}\). Let \((\vartheta_\ell)_{\ell\ge1}\) be a deterministic countable dense subset of \(K_N\), and let \(h_j(\vartheta)\) be target coordinate \(j\) of \((\Gamma m_c)_{c=1}^C\). Continuity of \(g\) and the reverse triangle inequality give
\[
d(x)=\min_{\vartheta\in K_N}\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m},
\qquad
|d(x)-d(y)|\le\|x-y\|_{\mathsf m}.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus \(d\) is continuous. For \(r>0\), define
\[
u_{j,k}(x,r)=\sup\left\{h_j(\vartheta_\ell):
\|g(\vartheta_\ell)-x\|_{\mathsf m}<d(x)+r+k^{-1},\ \ell\ge1\right\},
\tag{16}
\]
using \(-b_\lambda\) if the displayed set is empty. Each function in (16) is Borel measurable because it is a countable supremum of functions selected by open inequalities involving the continuous map \(d\). Compactness, continuity, and density imply
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\max_{\substack{\vartheta\in K_N:\\
\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m}\le d(x)+r}}h_j(\vartheta).
\tag{17}
\]
Indeed, dense approximation of any feasible point gives the lower inequality in (17); approximate maximizers on the left have a convergent subsequence in \(K_N\), whose limit satisfies the weak constraint and gives the reverse inequality. Applying the same argument to \(-h_j\) makes the raw lower endpoint measurable. The block medians \(\widehat\theta\) and \(\widehat v\), and hence the strictly positive \(\widehat\rho_N\), are measurable by \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}observed\text{-}moments}\). Substituting \((x,r)=(\widehat\theta,\widehat\rho_N)\) into (17), and then taking coordinatewise maxima and minima with the deterministic endpoints \(-b_\lambda\) and \(b_\lambda\), proves measurability of \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\) for \(N\ge2k_\alpha\). The small-sample box is deterministic, so measurability holds for every \(N\).

It remains to bound width. The feasible set \(\mathcal C_N\) is nonempty because a minimizer attaining \(d_N\) belongs to it. For arbitrary \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal C_N\), the triangle inequality and (13) give, without conditioning on \(\mathcal E_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}
&\le\|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
+\|g(\widetilde\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}\\
&\le2(d_N+\widehat\rho_N)
\le2(E_N+\widehat\rho_N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
Both parameters lie in \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\). Applying \(\mathrm{lem:observed\text{-}moment\text{-}inverse\text{-}modulus}\) to (18), and absorbing the factor two into its fixed constant, yields
\[
\max_{c\in[C]}
\|\Gamma m_c-\widetilde\Gamma\widetilde m_c\|_\infty
\le K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
The half-width of the coordinatewise enclosing rectangle is at most half the corresponding target-coordinate diameter, and intersection with a box cannot increase it. Equation (19), the definition of \(W\), and the box bound (6) therefore give the two simultaneous pointwise inequalities
\[
W(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})\le b_\lambda,
\qquad
W(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
\le K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}.
\tag{20}
\]
The function \(x\mapsto\min\{1,x\}\) is increasing and concave on \([0,\infty)\). Jensen's inequality and the expectation bound in \(\mathrm{lem:robust\text{-}moment\text{-}ball}\) imply, after enlarging constants depending only on \(\alpha\), the fixed primitive radii, and \((T,C)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
&\le K\min\!\left\{1,
\frac{\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P(E_N+\widehat\rho_N)}{s_N}\right\}\\
&\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
\]
The first inequality in (20) also gives
\(\sup_P\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})\le b_\lambda\). Combining this with (21) proves the asserted minimum bound for \(N\ge2k_\alpha\).

If \(N<2k_\alpha\), the fallback box has normalized maximal half-width \(\min\{1,b_\lambda\}\), which is at most \(b_\lambda\). Since \(s_N\le1\),
\[
\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\ge(2k_\alpha)^{-1/2}.
\tag{22}
\]
Choosing \(C_\alpha\ge\sqrt{2k_\alpha}\) makes the width at most the second term in the asserted minimum as well. This proves the width bound for every \(N\).

By (14) and the definition of \(\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\), the constructed rectangle belongs to \(\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\). Evaluating the infimum over honest rectangles at this rectangle gives the second displayed bound in the theorem. Finally, \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\) is deterministic and false whenever \(N\ge2k_\alpha\). Thus
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[W(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})1\{\mathsf F_N\}\right]=0
\quad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N),\ N\ge2k_\alpha.
\]
The ratio of this zero quantity to the positive scale \((\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\) is identically zero for every \(s_N\in(0,1]\), proving the stated uniform little-\(o\) conclusion.

Put \(q_0=4+\delta\). Under the displayed hypotheses of this lemma, \(v_\star=v\) and
\[
M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{q_0/2}=(2v_\star)^{q_0/2}.
\]
Consequently the definition of the effective loading-mean radius gives \(b_\lambda=0\). The zero-radius conclusion of \(\operatorname{lem:effective\text{-}loading\text{-}mean\text{-}radius\text{-}bound}\) applies to every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every \(c\in[C]\), and yields
\[
H_c=v_\star I_2=vI_2,
\qquad
m_c=0,
\qquad
\varepsilon_i=0\quad\text{almost surely conditional on }C_i=c,
\qquad
\mu_c(P)=0.
\]
In particular \(\mu(P)=0\). This proves the stated lemma. The proved sharp-radius lemma also shows that the equality \(v^\star=v_\star\) is not needed for the stronger zero-radius conclusion.

added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(c\in[C]\). The positive share restriction makes conditioning on \(C_i=c\) well defined. Write \(q_0=4+\delta>2\). By the definition of \(m_c\) and \(H_c\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\|\lambda_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c\right]
=\operatorname{tr}(H_c)+\|m_c\|_2^2.
\tag{1}
\]
Put \(r=q_0/2>1\). For every \(x\geq0\), elementary calculus applied to \(x^r-rx+(r-1)\) gives
\[
x\leq \frac{r-1}{r}+\frac{x^r}{r}.
\]
For a nonnegative random variable \(X\), apply this inequality to \(X/\{\mathbb E(X^r)\}^{1/r}\) when \(\mathbb E(X^r)>0\), and treat the zero-moment case directly. Taking expectations proves \(\{\mathbb E X\}^r\leq\mathbb E(X^r)\). Applying this result conditionally with \(X=\|\lambda_i\|_2^2\), and then applying the primitive moment bound, gives
\[
\left\{\operatorname{tr}(H_c)+\|m_c\|_2^2\right\}^{q_0/2}
\leq
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c\right]
\leq M_{\mathrm{mom}}.
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(H_c\succeq v_\star I_2\), its two eigenvalues are at least \(v_\star\), and hence
\[
\operatorname{tr}(H_c)\geq 2v_\star.
\tag{3}
\]
Raising (2) to the positive power \(2/q_0\), using (3), and subtracting \(2v_\star\) yield
\[
0\leq\|m_c\|_2^2
\leq M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-\operatorname{tr}(H_c)
\leq M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}-2v_\star.
\tag{4}
\]
Thus the rightmost quantity in (4) is nonnegative whenever \(P\in\mathcal M\), and the definition of \(b_\lambda\) gives \(\|m_c\|_2\leq b_\lambda\). The factor normalization \(\Gamma'\Gamma=I_2\) implies \(\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\). Since the outcome equation and the conditional mean-zero error restriction give \(\mu_c(P)=\Gamma m_c\),
\[
|\mu_{ct}(P)|
\leq\|\Gamma m_c\|_2
\leq\|\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|m_c\|_2
\leq b_\lambda.
\tag{5}
\]
This proves both radius bounds.

Suppose next that \(\mathcal M\) is nonempty. Choosing any \(P\in\mathcal M\), equations (2)--(3) imply
\[
M_{\mathrm{mom}}\geq(2v_\star)^{q_0/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
By the definition of the positive part, \(b_\lambda=0\) is equivalent to \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{2/q_0}\leq2v_\star\). Combining this inequality with (6), and using strict monotonicity of positive powers, proves
\[
b_\lambda=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v_\star)^{q_0/2}.
\tag{7}
\]

Assume the equivalent conditions in (7), fix again \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(c\in[C]\), and retain all nonnegative terms in the moment restriction. Equations (1)--(3) give the closed chain
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2v_\star)^{q_0/2}
=M_{\mathrm{mom}}
&\geq
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}+\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}
\mid C_i=c
\right]\\
&\geq
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c\right]\\
&\geq
\left\{\operatorname{tr}(H_c)+\|m_c\|_2^2\right\}^{q_0/2}\\
&\geq(2v_\star)^{q_0/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
The endpoints of (8) coincide, so every inequality in that chain is an equality. Strict monotonicity gives
\[
\operatorname{tr}(H_c)+\|m_c\|_2^2=2v_\star.
\tag{9}
\]
Both \(\operatorname{tr}(H_c)-2v_\star\) and \(\|m_c\|_2^2\) are nonnegative by (3), so (9) forces
\[
\operatorname{tr}(H_c)=2v_\star,
\qquad
m_c=0.
\tag{10}
\]
The matrix \(H_c-v_\star I_2\) is positive semidefinite and has trace zero by (10). Its eigenvalues are therefore nonnegative and sum to zero, so both vanish and
\[
H_c=v_\star I_2.
\tag{11}
\]
Equality between the first two expectation terms in (8) also gives
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c\right]=0.
\tag{12}
\]
The random variable in (12) is nonnegative; hence it is zero almost surely under the conditional law, which is equivalent to \(\varepsilon_i=0\) almost surely conditional on \(C_i=c\). Finally, \(\mu_c(P)=\Gamma m_c=0\) by (10). Since \(P\) and \(c\) were arbitrary, all conclusions hold throughout \(\mathcal M\).
